pct.$comment-danger: `danger` has no `on-danger` pair, because in this library it is not a SURFACE: it paints the message text and the error state's border, nothing else. The pair once hung here declared and used by no token and no stylesheet — that is, it looked like coverage that did not exist. It will return with the first component painting a background with the error colour (toast, badge), and then it will show in the diff.
pct.$comment-scrim: The veil a modal draws over the page, and the reason it is a SEMANTIC token rather than a value in a component sheet: how much a modal takes the page away is a property of the skin, not of the dialog. Here it is the ramp's darkest ordinary step — over a light page that reads as a dimming rather than as a blackout. The dark theme answers differently, which is the whole point of the tier.
